title: Ask HN: How to visually edit vibe coded websites?
summary:
I like building small sites (plain HTML/CSS/JS) for friends for their small businesses with Claude. It's easy and rewarding. Then I host them on Cloudflare or Netlify with a custom domain, basically free.

But then my friends want to update the text and swap pictures. They don't know GitHub or using ChatGpt with Github. Wix and Squarespace feel like overkill, and overpriced, for a few small edits a year.

I couldn't find a solution I liked, so I built a proof of concept that edits the Website content visually and pushes the changes back to GitHub. My friends liked it. Now I'm trying to make it usable for more people (https://editany.page/, currently a waitlist only), so I'm definitely biased. I am open to scrap this and join an open source imitative. I just could not find anything easy to use. And I don't want complicated react builds, or a markdown to static website pipeline.

I'd like to hear how you handle this.

Background: I know to build complex React web apps. But for most small sites, plain HTML/CSS/JS is just enough, plus an external form.

title: Tell HN: HN is being scraped for emails to scam
summary:
I know that many folks here post their personal emails in the Who's for Hire monthly pages and other places, and want to remind you that this public site gets views from folks with ill intent (or their bots/agents) as well. I use unique emails for every site, so I immediately knew that the late AWS payments email sent to my HN email were fake. There were other tells, but I want to remind everyone to be vigilant! HN is public but even social media sites where you supposedly can make your page private I've had some of those emails suddenly have spam sent to as well. Please be safe everyone!

My favorite tells that an email is a scam: - Before opening a surprising/suspicious email, hover over the sender name to see the domain the sender came from (don't open the email if it's strange). - _If_ you already opened the email, before clicking any links in the email, hover over them to see the domain that the link sends you to.

There are dozens more tips but a full article would be required, and these two will prevent you from falling for nearly all of them.

title: Ask HN: Do you have internet decision/emotional paralysis?
summary:
I often spend entire weekends doing nothing but watching Youtube and reading Hacker News. Maybe I read a book sometimes or play a game, but do nothing that is really an emotional important thing or decision. I think this has to do with how the internet and all these forms of media tend to take over your mind and numb your feelings.

Like at this moment as I'm writing this post, I have to really fight to take control over my mind and notice my own feelings and opinions about things rather than just open another post and read stuff. A lot of the time I read posts and watch YouTube videos and know nothing about what I feel about it, only see what other people think. Any thoughts on this? I can spend hours in this state, maybe a whole day without a single original thought or even analyzing a second hand thought.

title: Ask HN: Stripe closed us after one $1,500 invoice and never asked for evidence
summary:
We're a small business that sells pre-booked appointments with homeowners to local contractors, billed per appointment that actually happens.

Our first client agreed to this on a recorded call and saved his card through a $1 Stripe payment link, which we planned to use for billing later. That $1 payment went through.

A few weeks later we invoiced him $1,500 for 3 completed appointments and charged the saved card. Stripe blocked the payment. Two days after that the account was closed with this wording: payments "don't appear to have been authorized by the customer."

What happened next:

- We appealed through the Dashboard with an appeal letter, our company documents and the invoice. It was rejected the next day as an "unacceptable level of risk."

- Support told us our "business model presents a level of risk we're unable to support" and that the decision is final.

- After a Stripe employee escalated it internally, we got a short email saying Stripe still won't accept payments for our business.

In all of this, nobody asked us for the call recording, our messages with the client, or a confirmation from the client himself. As far as we know, he never disputed anything, and he has told us he is paying by bank transfer outside Stripe.

I'm not saying our setup is perfect. It's a new account, the first real charge was large compared to the $1 test, and billing a saved card later is probably what looked wrong. If there's something specific we should fix, I'll fix it.

What I'm asking:

1. Is there anyone at Stripe who can look at this with the evidence, including getting the client on a call?

2. For people who've been through this: how would you structure per-appointment billing so it doesn't look unauthorized (an invoice with a link each time, an email confirmation before each charge, something else)?

I can share the account details, the call recording and the messages with anyone from Stripe who wants to look. Thanks for reading.

title: Ask HN: Tips for maintainability of large software projects using agents?
summary:
Hey HN,

There is an interesting ongoing tension in the discourse around the quality of AI-generated code and whether "coding is solved".

As an experienced but very average programmer, the powers that AI have unlocked for me are nothing short of incredible. At work I am far more productive, and personally I have created/generated software that I would never have been able to create. For example, I've created my own very functional DAW (Digital Audio Workstation) that has tight integration with specific hardware I own.

I'm wondering if we are past the point of "AI generates bad and unmaintainable code". My gut tells me that for the most part we are, and my reasoning for this:

A) AI agents are able to find and fix many issues that I would never have caught B) They are FAR faster than me C) They generate WAY more tests (admittedly, sometimes it's out of hand) D) If something starts to really go sidewise in terms of code organization, you can often use AI to do the refactoring and cleanup and re-testing while you are out for a walk or having dinner with your family...

We are still fairly early into this experiment though. Do you fear that AI is generating unmaintainable code? Is the industry going to have major problems in the future with technical debt that more use of agents can't get us out of?

Do you have tips for how to coach agents into creating code that is correct and maintainable long term?

Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50508896
